newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK NBS TO SCRAP FOREIGN LOAN APPROVAL MEASURE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK NBS TO SCRAP FOREIGN LOAN APPROVAL MEASURE.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) will, by the end of this year, end a measure requiring firms seeking foreign loans of three years or longer to receive central bank approval, NBS vice-governor Marian Jusko said on Thursday.
Jusko said that by the end of this year the NBS also would cancel the obligation of approval for Slovak investments and loans made abroad with maturities of five and more years.
"This liberalisation of the foreign exchange regime is a part of our strategy in adjusting the foreign exchange environment according to OECD standards," Jusko told a conference in Bratislava.
Under current legislation, any foreign loan to a Slovak company must be approved by the NBS. The measure also applies to any direct investment or loan activities abroad by Slovaks.
Jusko said the liberalisation of the current foreign exchange regime would also include a lifting of the ban on foreigners buying real estate in Slovakia.
Slovakia is expected to become an OECD member in 1997.
